title: SpaceX Joins Nasdaq-100 in Fastest-Ever Index Inclusion After IPO
detail: SPCX joined the Nasdaq-100 index on July 7, 2026 — just 15 trading days after its June 12 Nasdaq debut, the fastest inclusion in the benchmark's history. The move was enabled by a Nasdaq rule change, announced June 26, that fast-tracks mega-cap IPOs into the index regardless of standard seasoning requirements. Despite a market capitalization around $2.3 trillion — comparable to Amazon's — SpaceX's initial index weighting is only about 1%, since weighting is based on free-float market cap that excludes Musk's large insider stake. The addition was expected to drive roughly $4.3 billion in passive buying as the roughly $800 billion in Nasdaq-100-tracking funds, led by Invesco's QQQ, rebalanced to include the stock.

title: Transporter-17 Rideshare Launches First Commercial Nuclear-Powered Satellite, Tops 1,800 Rideshare Payloads
detail: SpaceX's Transporter-17 dedicated smallsat rideshare mission lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 3:12 a.m. ET on July 7, 2026, carrying 81 payloads on a Falcon 9 and pushing SpaceX's cumulative rideshare payload count past 1,800 since the Transporter program began. The manifest included City Labs' BOHR CubeSat, the first commercial nuclear-powered satellite and first nuclear CubeSat ever flown, demonstrating the company's proprietary NanoTritium betavoltaic technology as a continuous power source independent of solar panels. The Falcon 9 first stage landed on a drone ship in the Pacific roughly 8.5 minutes after liftoff.
